text:
sanjay: Heads up — we're seeing p95 east-west latency spike ~600ms between gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-29 during today's 11:40-12:05 batching window. Affects ~12 pods serving generation requests. Observed RX drops on both NICs and intermittent RDMA QP errors.

marta: Ugh. Can you grab ethtool -S, ibv_devinfo, and a brief tcpdump from both nodes? Also which ToR are they on?

sanjay: quick dumps attached (snips below). ToR: tor-west-3.

```
# ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "rx_|tx_|drop"
rx_no_buffer: 12456
rx_missed_errors: 312
tx_errors: 0
rx_crc_errors: 0

# ibv_devinfo -v mlx5_0 | grep -E "active_qps|port\|link_rate"
active_qps: 240
port 1:
    state: PORT_ACTIVE
    phys_state: LINK_UP

# rdma stats (psm2): qp0 rx_err=14 rx_compl_timeout=0
```

# tcpdump (abridged)
```
11:42:05.123456 IP 10.240.3.12.43912 > 10.240.7.29.32000: Flags [P.], seq 1:120, ack 1, win 1234, length 119
11:42:05.223567 IP 10.240.3.12 > 10.240.7.29: icmp seq=1 Destination unreachable
11:42:05.323678 IP 10.240.3.12.43912 > 10.240.7.29.32000: Flags [P.], seq 120:240, ack 1, length 120
(repeat bursts ~every 10-20ms during peak)
```

clara: RX_missed_errors look bad. Could be NIC buffer exhaustion on the ToR uplink or a driver/firmware bug triggered by the sustained tiny-packet bursts from batching. We've seen similar with LRO/GRO before.

kai: Agree. Quick mitigation: try disabling GRO/GSO/LRO on the workload host NICs and the ToR if possible. Also validate if RDMA tunneling (PSM2 over Ethernet) is exposing a bug.

devops-jen: Can we divert traffic to spare racks while we investigate? I can shift a couple of batch queues to spare-gpu-pool-2 but that's capacity-limited. Would prefer a non-disruptive fix if possible.

sanjay: Did the GRO/GSO test on one pair: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` — p95 dropped from ~600ms to ~85ms in the isolated experiment. No errors in RDMA counters for that pair during the window.

nate: That strongly points at aggregation/GRO path. Hypothesis: ToR NIC or firmware mis-handles bursty small packets under RDMA/Verbs -> causes RX drop spikes, which then inflate retrans and increase latency.

marta: Good repro signal. Next steps: 1) Enable GRO/GSO off as temporary mitigation for affected rack via daemonset on infra nodes, 2) Capture full firmware/driver versions and file vendor ticket (include tcpdump + ethtool -S + ib stats), 3) Schedule ToR firmware rollback/upgrade window if vendor confirms.

kai: I'll own vendor ticket. Taking host logs + firmware versions now: mlx5 driver 5.15.0-rt, fw 16.26.1020.

clara: Also adding a short-term autoscale throttle to batching controller to smooth the concurrency ramp — lowers probability of hitting the failure mode while we wait on hardware vendor.

oncall-bot: Incident created #INC-2026-847. Pager duty: @kai on call.

marta: Thanks everyone. I'll update the incident with the GRO/GSO experiment and attach the snippets. Post-mortem will include checklist for "batch burst" networking tests and a runbook entry to flip GRO on/off per-rack.

sanjay: TL;DR: root cause hypothesis = NIC/ToR buffer handling bug with GRO/LRO under RDMA-heavy small-packet bursts. Workaround applied (GRO off) reduced p95 by ~7x. Vendor ticket and capacity throttles in flight.
